_status: Literature-derived parameter RANGES for PM-001 (research synthesis, 2026-10-30). NOT POLLEN measurements: no measured POLLEN Cd, Cl(S), spin decay, COR, friction or N(delta) exists anywhere (research/checks/sweep_pollen.md). Same layout as data/aero_params.json so src/flight.load_params(path=...) reads it (extra Cl set 'floor'; use which={'Cl':'floor'}); launcher and contact blocks are extra and not read by src/. Each entry has grade (A-D, see grades), source_ids (see sources) and vs_PM001 (how the current data/aero_params.json, data/launch_envelope.json or src/contact.py value compares). See research/LITERATURE_SYNTHESIS.md.

grades.A: peer-reviewed original measurement, transferable to POLLEN
grades.B: peer-reviewed but different ball/regime, or model/theory only
grades.C: preprint, unreviewed web article, vendor data or forum data with numbers
grades.D: anecdote/observation, or assumption with no source

rho.prov: standard air property, unchanged from data/aero_params.json

mass.vs_PM001: high bound too low (PM-001 26.5 g; vendor listing weight 27.2 g)
mass.prov: AndyMark spec 0.055 lb = 24.95 g; Shopify variant weight 27.2 g (listing/shipping weight, grade D); CAD shell at PE density 20.5-22.0 g. high widened to 27.5 g. Weigh >=10 balls.

radius.prov: manual 'approximately 2.8 in (7.1 cm)'; print OD 2.8 in; CAD R 1.40 in

geometry_from_cad.prov: STEP parsed by the sweep_pollen checker; print reads .4 (26), STEP 0.44 in; molded balls may differ (mass).

I_b.vs_PM001: inside (high raised only to follow the 27.5 g mass bound)
I_b.prov: thick-shell 0.4(Ro^5-Ri^5)/((Ro^3-Ri^3)Ro^2) = 0.634 (1.78 mm wall), 0.629 (2.1 mm). Cross 2002: real tennis ball alpha 0.55 (thick 6 mm rubber wall); POLLEN wall/R ~0.05 so 0.55 is not expected; launcher k_I low 0.55 is pessimistic but harmless. Measure with a rolling incline: a = g sin(th)/(1+alpha).

Re_range_note: Re = vD/nu, D 0.071 m: 2-10 m/s -> 9.5e3-4.7e4. This OVERLAPS the smooth-sphere LIFT-crisis band (Sakai/Miyazaki table-tennis wind tunnel Re 3e4-5e4 dips; Ito & Kamijima CFD 2.65e4-5.3e4; Sareen 1e3-5e4) but lies below the drag crisis and below every documented negative-Magnus window (Maccoll >= 4.6e4 at S < 0.6; Taneda 6e4+; Muto LES 2e5). Pickleball free-flight data cover Re 2.95e4-5.67e4 (Lindsey, 6.0-11.5 m/s) and 4.7e4-6.1e4 (Steyn); Van Wyk lab tests (method per Lyu et al. 2025, not described in the paper) 7.7e4-1.4e5.

Cd.model: constant per run; optional spin term Cd = Cd0 + dCd*min(S/0.6, 1), dCd 0-0.15 (smooth-sphere evidence that spin raises Cd)
Cd.vs_PM001: nominal 0.48 inside; high 0.65 OPTIMISTIC (too little drag for a spinning perforated ball); low 0.35 fine
Cd.prov: 26-hole indoor pickleball free flight 0.45 (SD 0.09) but the same author's hole-modification control ball reads 0.59-0.985 (fit 0.65-0.82) at 6.2-8.25 m/s and taping the holes gives ~0.43 (Lindsey, C); 40-hole outdoor 0.33 (Lindsey) and 0.30+/-0.02 (Steyn, n=6); pickleball lab tests ~0.40 at Re 7.7e4-1.4e5 (Van Wyk, B; method per Lyu et al. 2025, not described in the paper); Wiffle 0.36-1.05 by orientation and Re, rising toward ~1 at the lowest Re (Rossmann & Rau, full text, B); smooth spinning sphere 0.45-0.62 (Ito CFD), 0.474 (S 0.2) / 0.661 (S 1.0) (Muto LES; authors flag subcritical disagreement); 2017 FRC FUEL drop test recomputed 0.88 (D).

Cl.formula: Cl = min(c1*S, Cl_max); run 'floor' as the pessimistic bound and dip_variant as a structural check

floor.note: Lindsey backspin fit |Cl| = 0.173 + 0.02 S (S <= 0.37): if the 0.17 offset is not spin lift (the source cannot tell; both worked examples are topspin), the Magnus part is ~0.02 S. Also represents 'holes vent the lift away'. Replaces PM-001's informal Cl = 0 floor.

low.note: Steyn 0.195 S (40-hole, S <= 0.3); cap = deepest smooth-sphere crisis trough in POLLEN's Re band (Ito 0.153-0.207; Sakai valleys 0.09-0.21).

nominal.note: between pickleball slopes (0.20-0.47 per unit S) and smooth (0.8-1.0); cap between smooth trough (~0.18-0.21) and smooth S ~1 values (0.30-0.33). Unchanged from PM-001.

high.note: smooth initial slope 0.8-1.0; Ito max 0.42 (Re 6.6e3); Cross 2012 polystyrene plateau 0.33; Vilumbrales 0.35-0.40 (Re 7e4-1e5). Unchanged; Van Wyk 0.0124+0.466 S gives 0.27 at S 0.56 (end of its data) so 0.40 is generous.

dip_variant.description: smooth-sphere lift crisis (Ito & Kamijima 2025 CFD; Sakai 2016 wind tunnel) at Re ~4e4: Cl(S) = interp(S, S_pts, Cl_pts); scale the table by 0.5-1.0 for venting. Not read by src/flight.py.

negative_magnus.probability: low at POLLEN Re: documented negative-lift windows are Re >= 4.6e4 at S < 0.6, mostly 1e5-2e5. Not excluded: perforated-ball lift data stop at S ~0.56 in backspin (Van Wyk) and S ~0.65 in topspin (Lindsey, unreviewed).

non_magnus_hole_force.units: Cl-equivalent; random direction per shot for a non-spinning ball; averages out per revolution for a spinning ball (mainly scatter)
non_magnus_hole_force.note: Wiffle one-sided slots: -0.15 to +0.145, sign change near Re 5.5e4. POLLEN's 26 holes are near-uniform, so a smaller value is expected.

Cl.vs_PM001: nominal and high inside; PM-001 low (0.15 S, cap 0.10) is NOT the pessimistic bound: add 'floor' (0.02 S, cap 0.04) and run dip_variant
Cl.prov: see sets; reasoning in research/LITERATURE_SYNTHESIS.md section 3

spin_decay_k.model: preferred: d(omega)/dt = -(pi rho beta R^2 |v| / (alpha m)) omega = -0.30 beta |v| omega; constant k: nominal 0.03 is the |v| ~5 m/s equivalent of beta 0.02; low 0.005 and high 0.15 are the beta_low at |v| ~2 m/s and beta_high at |v| ~10 m/s extremes
spin_decay_k.vs_PM001: nominal 0.05 inside; high 0.30 beyond any evidence (pessimistic); low 0.01 inside
spin_decay_k.prov: golf beta 0.009-0.012 (Smits & Smith; Tavares; via Nathan); Ito smooth-sphere moment C_M = (3/8)Cl/S scaled to POLLEN: k 0.011-0.023 /s; Cross 2012 saw no measurable decay in 0.7 s. Paddle effect of holes: beta to ~0.05 is a guess. 1.2 s flight: 0.6% / 3.5% / 17% spin loss. Second-order next to Cl.

launcher.model_to_adopt: keep src/launcher.py (2x2 LCP stick/slip contact) and unit-test it against the Pedersen rigid limit (Brettle is the special case G = 0, k_p = k_w = 1/2-type inertias); add a hood no-slip check |H_h| <= mu_hood N

S_exit_hood.vs_PM001: inside (envelope 1.03-1.27 at 3000 rpm); values above ~1.3 need mu_hood < ~0.1
S_exit_hood.prov: rigid rolling on a gripping hood S = 1; compression S = R/(R - lambda delta/2) = 1.03-1.13; frictionless hood S = 1/k = 1.5-1.67. Theory only: no published spin measurement of any single-wheel hooded shooter.

S_exit_passive_roller.vs_PM001: inside (envelope 0.91-1.24); S < 1 only transiently (heavy roller lag)
S_exit_passive_roller.prov: a free roller removes the hood's forward friction impulse so S moves from 1 toward 1/k; it cannot reduce spin below ~1.

v_over_surface_speed.vs_PM001: PM-001 hood_nominal ~0.46-0.47 below the grip limit is on the optimistic side
v_over_surface_speed.prov: ideal 0.5 (rigid, no slip, infinite I_w); FRC slow-motion and forum estimates 0.30-0.45 on other balls.

energy_knockdown_vs_rigid.vs_PM001: not in src (hysteresis c_rr covers part)
energy_knockdown_vs_rigid.prov: Pedersen forum: real tennis-ball KE ~56% of the rigid prediction; Brettle: compression drains more wheel speed than predicted. Use as a KE multiplier when comparing to tests.

mu_hood.vs_PM001: same; unsourced. Use a sliding (in-contact) mu: Cross found the in-bounce mu ~3x below the quasi-static value for a gripping tennis ball at 45 deg

N_delta.law: piecewise: linear Reissner ramp up to delta ~ wall thickness, then softening/buckling plateau of unknown height (not Hertz)

reissner_per_contact.E_note: PE modulus range from memory, unverified
reissner_per_contact.valid_for: per-contact delta <~ t = 1.8 mm, intact shell (holes lower it)

N_at_4mm_N.vs_PM001: PM-001 linear k_n 1.5-10 N/mm (N(4 mm) 6-40 N) sits far below the intact-shell Reissner slope; holes and buckling lower the real value by an unknown amount, so the high end is widened

N_delta.effect: N sets the grip-limited top speed and flywheel drain; it barely changes S

contact.model_to_adopt: Walton/Brach impulse with Coulomb cap as in src/contact.py; it equals the Cross 2005 e_x model when e_t = e_x and contact grips. Keep the cap |P_t| <= mu P_n; e_x < 0 arises automatically in the slip branch.

e_n.prov: pickleball flat-plate COR 0.20 at 26.8 m/s (Van Wyk, 3-9x POLLEN's impact speed; polymer-shell COR rises at low speed) is a lower-bound proxy; tennis ~0.75 (Cross). No POLLEN value. Pickleball drop-spec COR ~0.62-0.66 is from memory, unverified. Drop test e = sqrt(h2/h1).

e_t.vs_PM001: default 0 inside; the 0.3 sensitivity variant is above every hollow-ball value (optimistic for spin reversal)
e_t.prov: tennis gripping bounces 0.10-0.24 (max ~0.2 near 50 deg); ~0.06 near-normal on a heavy rigid surface; < 0 when sliding throughout. Superball 0.49-0.76 (solid rubber) does not apply. Grade A for tennis balls; POLLEN transfer is a judgement.

mu_impact.prov: Allen: mu matters only in the sliding regime (shallow impacts); gripping bounces are mu-insensitive. Use a sliding-bounce mu.

spin_retained_near_normal.formula: omega2/omega1 = (alpha - e_x)/(1 + alpha) + (1 + e_x)/(1 + alpha) * v_x1/(R omega1)

rim_capture_effect_of_backspin.value: backspin helps capture on long rolling rim contacts; ~+10% makes in a basketball model; outcome very sensitive to contact point
rim_capture_effect_of_backspin.prov: basketball on a round rim; POLLEN in a box-shaped CELL is far from this; qualitative only

observed_bounce_out_POLLEN.prov: FTC 14343 fixed solid hood, spin not measured, distance/side not stated; bins do not reconcile (42 vs 43)
